clue.text: Main pressure contains opening of main sewer

indicators.note: contains means the two words for main and pressure hold a letter between them

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea
stress is pressure or strain

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A water-main under pressure holds the start of the main drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain, but it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sews for a living is literally one who stitches, a sewer.

clue.text: Reportedly so poorly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, a word with the same sound

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus or so, printed after a quoted error

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling poorly is British for being unwell, ill.

clue.text: Share everything outrageous describing blokes

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing a line around, so one word encloses another

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous
blokes are men

explanation.surface: An outrageous description of men takes all the share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of tracing a line round something.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a portion or share allotted to someone.

clue.text: Start of Stones' 'Stony' track

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: stony, as in stony-broke, means poor

explanation.surface: The opening of a Rolling Stones song called Stony makes a good track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stony' is short for stony-broke, i.e. penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail or footprints left by an animal, a track.

clue.text: Refuse work from cleric after massage

indicators.note: after puts the shortened cleric behind the word for massage

parts.note: to rub is to massage

indicators.note: work from cleric means the work is taken away from the cleric's word

parts.note: a bishop is a senior cleric
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A cleric declines to work after having a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes OP (opus, a work) from BISHOP, leaving BISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is waste or garbage, which is rubbish.

clue.text: They fix tiles eventually on board

indicators.note: on here means placed aboard, so the word for eventually sits within the ship

parts.note: to be on board is to be on a ship, and SS is a steamship
later means eventually

explanation.surface: Roofers get the tiles fixed eventually, working up on the boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for putting a word inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaters are tradesmen who lay roofing slates, tiles of stone.

clue.text: World is circumnavigated snatching record

indicators.note: snatching means the words grab a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: A round-the-world sailor snatches a world record.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a disc of vinyl.

clue.text: This compiler's mature figure

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves; this compiler is, I'm
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a grown-up physique.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a figure or likeness, such as a statue.

clue.text: Bless strange ancestor buried in church

indicators.note: buried in puts the jumbled word inside the church's letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: A curious ancestor lies interred in a churchyard, receiving a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the usual crossword church.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to make holy, to bless with sacred rites.

clue.text: Group with ordinary instrument

parts.note: a cell is a small group, as in a terrorist cell
O stands for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A band played an ordinary instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a bowed string instrument played between the knees.

clue.text: Awkwardly sat in bow clutching a sailor

indicators.note: clutching means the jumbled letters hold the single letter
awkwardly signals the words are rearranged clumsily

explanation.surface: Someone sits uncomfortably in the bow of a boat, gripping on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' rearranges SAT IN BOW, which 'clutching' wraps around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain is a ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew, a sailor.

clue.text: Copper's upset over rogue receiving zero help

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the S of the possessive

indicators.note: receiving means one word takes another inside it

parts.note: a cur is a scoundrel or rogue
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A policeman is upset to find a criminal taking nothing in aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal Cu; 'upset' reverses CUS to SUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is aid given in time of need, help.

clue.text: Engine burnt out absorbing current energy

indicators.note: absorbing means the jumbled letters take in another letter
out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A motor has burnt out after taking in current energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BURNT to TURBN, which takes in I, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a rotary engine driven by a flow of fluid.

clue.text: Initially circle round East Timor encircling island

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Sailing directions: go round East Timor, circling the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' at the end is the definition; East Timor is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Attractive Democrat attractive to voters?

parts.note: a candidate attractive to voters is electable

explanation.surface: A Democrat candidate is good-looking and will win votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delightful or appealing, attractive.

clue.text: Rot seen in European trees

parts.note: two trees, the yew and the ash

explanation.surface: Rot has been spotted in trees across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like decay of the trees, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or humbug, the same as rot in British slang.

clue.text: Old canine barking on time

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the next
barking means mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: An elderly dog barking on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for crazy, here an anagram signal for CANINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something ancient belongs to the distant past, very old.

clue.text: Empty samovar to hold endless drink one guzzles

indicators.note: to hold means the outer letters wrap round the shortened drink
empty means take out the middle, leaving the first and last letters
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: coffee is a drink

explanation.surface: An empty tea urn has to hold a drink that someone is gulping.
explanation.walkthrough: A samovar is a Russian tea urn; emptied it leaves only its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it greedily, so one who guzzles is described.

clue.text: Sycophant is more prostrate before Queen

indicators.note: before in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: flatter means lying more flat, more prostrate
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A toady grovels lower than anyone before the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns with insincere praise, like a flatterer.

clue.text: Go in for captivating single cold temptress?

indicators.note: captivating means taking captive, so one word holds others

parts.note: to go in is to enter
I is the Roman numeral for one, single
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An unmarried, frosty woman goes in for seduction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: a temptress is one sort of enticer.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptress lures and entices, an example of one who tempts.

clue.text: Rowdy rugby supporter going outside if promoted

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

indicators.note: going outside means the supporter's word wraps round other letters

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue means moved upward, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A rugby fan becomes rowdy outside, if his team is promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowdy' reads as an adjective but here is a noun, a rowdy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy as a noun is a rough, noisy person, a ruffian or thug.

clue.text: Fruit tart having spread inside

indicators.note: having inside means the first word holds the second

parts.note: tart means curt, sharp in manner
ran, as ink or butter ran, spread

explanation.surface: A fruit tart with a filling spread inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry, but it means sharp-tongued, CURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is a small dried grape or soft berry, a fruit.

clue.text: Scent of pine outgrowth around trunk

indicators.note: around means the outgrowth's word goes round the trunk's word

parts.note: a pine cone grows on a pine tree
a log is a section of tree trunk

explanation.surface: The smell of pine cones around a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne, eau de cologne, is a light perfume, a scent.

clue.text: Leader of Tories ready for nonsense

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter

parts.note: ripe means ready, as fruit is

explanation.surface: The Conservative leader is primed to talk nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal, but colloquially it means rubbish, nonsense.

clue.text: Clumsy in record time

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A clumsy athlete still sets a record time.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, awkward, clumsy.

clue.text: Disobey accepting a large after-effect

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes in the others

parts.note: to flout a rule is to disobey it
L stands for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: Ignoring orders by taking a big drink has consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallout is radioactive debris and, figuratively, any unpleasant after-effect.

clue.text: China's overlaid with old gems

indicators.note: overlaid with in a down clue puts the second piece on top of the first

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so china's is pal's

explanation.surface: Porcelain is decorated with antique jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain but is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones.

clue.text: Lifeless old man embraces sweetheart

indicators.note: embraces means the father's word wraps round the letter

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A frail elderly man hugs his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless means having died, no longer living.

clue.text: It's inspiring swimming round reef occasionally

indicators.note: round means the swimming word goes round other letters

parts.note: bathing in the sea is swimming

indicators.note: occasionally means take alternate letters

explanation.surface: Swimming over a reef is a wonderful, uplifting experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' reads as uplifting but means drawing breath in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration is the act of inhaling, so drawing in air is part of respiration.

clue.text: Concur and get on without hollow remorse

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round another

parts.note: to age is to get on in years

indicators.note: hollow means remove the middle, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Agree and carry on without any empty regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' looks like a second definition but is AGE, getting older; 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share an opinion, to be of one mind.

clue.text: Metal test periodically corrodes

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A metal test shows how often it corrodes.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid eats away metal, so it corrodes it.

clue.text: Dancing nudes once about right for adults?

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the letter
dancing signals the letters move around

explanation.surface: Nudes once danced, but is that right for grown-ups?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges NUDES ONCE around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Material shown uncut, without censorship, is often deemed suitable only for grown-ups.
